plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers on slender stems. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is widely grown in gardens and for commercial oil production.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France, England, and cultivated across temperate zones worldwide
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years in perfumes, bathing, and medicine; the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub producing large rounded clusters of showy flowers. Blooms open in early summer and persist for weeks, making it a staple of cottage and woodland gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely cultivated in the eastern United States, Europe, the Azores, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with floating round leaves and fragrant, star-shaped white flowers that rest on the water's surface. Flowers open in the morning and close in the afternoon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to late summer (June to August)
plants.location: Ponds, lakes, and slow rivers across Europe, North Africa, and parts of western Asia
plants.funFact: The flower stalks can grow several meters long to reach the surface, and the blooms track the sun, opening and closing in a daily rhythm.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the genus, a bowl-shaped bloom of pointed pink bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy florets. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak blooms from May to August
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa, in fynbos shrublands
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, reflecting the many forms of proteas.
